claims.text: Silicon carbide is a wide-bandgap semiconductor.
Introducing SRO precipitates into SiC will enhance phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering from SRO precipitates will decrease the lattice thermal conductivity of SiC.
The proposed initial material is high-quality, single-crystal SiC with minimal inherent SRO precipitates.
Controlled doping and/or thermal processing can introduce SRO precipitates and modulate their density and distribution in SiC.
Phonon transport dominates and electronic heat-transport contributions are negligible under the proposed room-temperature to moderately high-temperature conditions.
The relevant structural mediator is the density and distribution of SRO precipitates embedded in the SiC lattice.
SRO precipitates create local lattice distortions and strain fields in SiC.
The lattice distortions and strain fields associated with SRO precipitates scatter phonons.
Scattering by SRO precipitates reduces phonon mean free paths and lifetimes.
Reduced phonon mean free paths and lifetimes lower the lattice component of thermal conductivity.
Increasing SRO precipitate density will produce a measurable, systematic reduction in SiC lattice thermal conductivity relative to pristine SiC.
The proposed baseline is lattice thermal conductivity measured in pristine SiC without engineered SRO precipitates.
Significant electronic conduction could obscure the proposed effect on lattice thermal conductivity.
SRO precipitates that are too large may not effectively scatter phonons.
Time-domain thermoreflectance can be used in the proposed experiment to measure thermal conductivity while isolating the phonon contribution.
Electron microscopy can characterize the density and distribution of the proposed SRO precipitates.
